citation: Underwood & Underwood, State St., Chicago, Ill. (N. from Adams): noonday crowds on a thoroughfare 18 miles long, stereograph, copyright 1903 Mar. 26. Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division, Stereograph Cards, LC-DIG-stereo-1s12706 (item 2014650313).
author: Underwood & Underwood
repository: Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division. Master TIFF 1s12706u.tif (5860 x 3045), read at tile.loc.gov.
locator: The left-hand frame, the east sidewalk below the C. D. Peacock sign: men walking towards and away from the camera at roughly eight to fifteen metres.
rights_note: LOC rights advisory: 'No known restrictions on publication.' Published 1903. Used only as a reference picture people are judged against and for what men wore on a Chicago street (T-3441); nothing is traced or sampled from it.
access_notes: Viewed 2026-11-07 (T-3441) from the master TIFF. Noon on State Street at Adams, looking north, from above. Nearly every man wears a black derby; their coats are dark, most of them sack coats and overcoats, one in the centre a knee-length frock coat with a pale bow tie; trousers are mid to dark grey. The figures read as dark columns with pale faces and collars, the way a figure in the town reads at ten metres.
note: The far picture of the 1904 gentleman reference set (data/people_match/reference_sets/gentleman_1904.json): Chicago in the scene's decade.
what_it_supplies: that a Chicago businessman of 1903 wore a black derby by day, with a frock coat as well as with a sack coat
how dark coats, grey trousers and a white collar read on walking men at ten metres and more
what_it_does_not_supply: the cut of any garment in detail; any named person; no likeness is asserted
